alignments.note: כְּמוֹ is the predicate of a verbless wish; the italic Let ... be is the construction-supplied copula with its volitive auxiliary and joins the preposition's unit (rule 49), headed on as.
Supplied subject pronoun; the verse writes no nominal denoting the wicked, so no morpheme answers to it (rule 20's closing sentence, rule 25).
Supplied a belongs to the noun (rule 15).
Relative supplied over an asyndetic clause juxtaposed to the written antecedent snail (rules 46, 55).
Noun 'melting' rendered as the finite melteth.
Coordinator supplied where the Hebrew writes no waw (rule 14).
Verb rendered passeth away; away completes the lexeme in this idiom (rule 44).

נֵפֶל stands bare, with no preposition and no object marker, as the second simile; the italic Like the ASV writes before it states what that nominal contributes and belongs to the noun under rule 33 (as the comparative as of פַּלְגֵי מַיִם → as the watercourses does), not added. It is not a distributed repetition of the first כְּמוֹ under rule 25/33, since the Hebrew coordinates nothing under that preposition (no waw) and the ASV wrote a different word. Supplied the joins the construct noun (rule 29); birth alone is any birth, so the head goes on untimely (rule 31); birth was the competing head. Competing readings: Like added, or Like as the first כְּמוֹ's repeated scope.
Relative supplied over an asyndetic finite clause juxtaposed to a written antecedent (rules 46, 55). Margin (like them that have not seen the sun) read and set aside.
Perfect with its auxiliary hath seen, discontinuous around the negative (rule 25).
Supplied the belongs to the noun (rule 15).

review_notes: Corrected: the italic Like before the untimely birth was marked added; under rule 33 a comparative word the ASV supplies before a bare nominal it construes as a comparison belongs to that nominal, so it now joins נֵפֶל's unit. Other supplied connectives and relatives (them, which, and, that) remain added on their own.
